summary: On the main deck, Neo is plugged in and hanging in a suspension chair while Tank, settling into his operator's chair, complains that loading all the operations programs first is boring and proposes starting with something fun instead. Tank flips through a carousel of micro discs and suggests combat training. Neo reads the disk label and realizes he is he will be taught jujitsu. Tank inserts the disk into Neo's supplement drive; Neo says no way, but Tank smiles and punches the load code. Neo's body jumps against the harness, neo's eyes snap shut, the monitors go haywire as his heart hammers and brain sizzles, then his eyes snap open and he exclaims holy shit. Tank jokes that Mikey likes it and asks if he is ready for more, and Neo answers hell yes.

what_changes.before: Obligated to follow the proper training order, he grumbles that "Protocol demands we run the ops routines first, yet this is dreadfully dull."
what_changes.after: He abandons the prescribed order for his own amusement: "Why don't we kick things off with something a bit more entertaining?"
what_changes.evidence: We're supposed to load all these operations

what_changes.before: He has no combat skills loaded and reacts with disbelief on reading the disk: "Jujitsu? I'm going to learn jujitsu?"
what_changes.after: After the program is loaded into him, he has the skill and is thrilled by it: "Holy shit!" ... "Hell yes!"
what_changes.evidence: Tank slides the disk into Neo's supplement

event_hint.one_line: Tank loads a jujitsu combat program into Neo, giving him the skill instantly.

uncertain: Whether the disk Neo reads the label on is the same disk Tank slides into Neo's supplement drive, or a separate one.

minds.wants: To make Neo's training fun for himself — to skip the prescribed 'operations programs' and get to the good part (combat) rather than grind through boring basics.
minds.feels: Genuinely excited and curious, both about the sheer novelty of teaching and about the chance to see what the supposed 'One' can actually do. Under the clowning is real investment in Neo as a test of the prophecy.
minds.shows: A casual, irreverent operator who treats the loading as a game — complaining about the boring stuff, grinning, punching 'load' over Neo's weak 'No way,' and cracking the 'Hey Mikey' cereal-jingle joke.
minds.basis: He opens by dismissing the required order ('this is some major boring shit') and proposing 'something a little fun,' then flips the carousel and loads jujitsu while smiling despite Neo's 'No way.' His 'Ready for more?' and the Mikey joke show him enjoying the process. In sc-047 he already told Neo he's 'pretty eager to find out what you can do.'

believes_about.belief: That Neo is a promising blank slate he gets to shape — possibly the One — and that the training will be a fun reveal of hidden capability.
believes_about.wrong_because: He is treating this as a game and a spectacle, not yet knowing how much Neo will actually struggle and suffer (the later brutal sparring and the terror of the jump), so his lightness is partly a miscalibration of what's coming.

minds.wants: To acquire the skill he's just been told he needs — and, in this moment, to get past disbelief into actually having it.
minds.feels: A rush of disbelief turning into exhilaration: the absurdity of learning 'jujitsu' by loading a disc, then the overwhelming physical shock of the download, resolving into pure, almost giddy empowerment ('Holy shit! ... Hell yes!').
minds.shows: First a disbelieving question on reading the label, then a token protest ('No way') that he doesn't enforce, then an involuntary physical reaction to the load, and finally open delight and eagerness for more.
minds.basis: He reads the label and reacts with disbelief ('Jujitsu? I'm going to learn jujitsu?'), offers a half-hearted 'No way' that Tank rides right past, then after the load — body jumping, eyes clamping shut, monitors kicking — he exclaims 'Holy shit!' and immediately answers 'Hell yes!' when asked if he wants more.

believes_about.belief: That Tank's playfulness means the training is easy and safe — a fun shortcut.
believes_about.wrong_because: Tank's ease is personality, not a promise; the ease of the *download* masks how hard the *application* will be, and Neo has not yet met Morpheus's physical superiority or his own fear.

believes_about.belief: That this instantaneous acquisition means he's now genuinely skilled — that possessing the knowledge equals being able to use it.
believes_about.wrong_because: The scene gives him the program but not mastery; the coming sparring will show that 'knowing' kung fu/jujitsu and defeating Morpheus are entirely different things.

connects_back: Morpheus's sc-045 promise that Neo is 'going to need' rest 'for your training' — this scene is the training beginning.
Tank's sc-047 self-introduction as operator ('I'll be your operator') and his stated excitement to 'see what you are capable of,' which motivates his eagerness here.
Tank's sc-047 'There's much to accomplish, so let's begin.,' realized as the actual loading session.
sets_up: The instant, almost magical acquisition of skill (jujitsu) establishes the download-as-learning mechanic that the ten-hour combat training relies on and that makes Neo's later physical exhaustion believable.
Neo's 'Hell yes!' eagerness and quick delight set up his confidence going into sparring, which Morpheus will then dismantle physically.
Tank's willingness to bypass the prescribed order for fun foreshadows his role as the operator who will run Neo's combat and jump programs.
The visceral, pleasurable shock of the load primes the audience (and Neo) for the later, less pleasant downloads (the rooftop-jump program) and the bodily cost of training.
dramatic_function: It converts the prophecy's abstract promise into a concrete, pleasurable proof-of-concept — the audience and Neo experience the Matrix's rules bending for him — while characterizing Tank's buoyant optimism and Neo's hunger, so that the ease and triumph here make the difficulty and failure of the coming sparring land harder.
